officialTitle: Adagrasib in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer Harboring a KRAS G12C Mutation

design.blinding: Open-label; response by blinded independent central review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: As of October 15, 2021, a total of 116 patients with-mutated NSCLC had been treated (median follow-up, 12.9 months)
design.notes: Registrational phase 2 cohort of the phase 1-2 KRYSTAL-1 study.

clinicalQuestion: What is the activity of adagrasib in KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC previously treated with chemotherapy and anti-PD-(L)1 therapy?

pico.population: KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC previously treated with platinum chemotherapy and anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy
pico.outcomes: Primary: BICR ORR. Secondary: DoR, PFS, OS, safety

arms.label: Adagrasib
arms.doseSourceQuote: we evaluated adagrasib (600 mg orally twice daily)

publications.title: Adagrasib in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer Harboring aMutation.
publications.label: Registrational phase 2 cohort

outcomes.sourceQuote: Of 112 patients with measurable disease at baseline, 48 (42.9%) had a confirmed objective response.
The median duration of response was 8.5 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 6.2 to 13.8), and the median progression-free survival was 6.5 months (95% CI, 4.7 to 8.4).
The median duration of response was 8.5 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 6.2 to 13.8), and the median progression-free survival was 6.5 months (95% CI, 4.7 to 8.4).
As of January 15, 2022 (median follow-up, 15.6 months), the median overall survival was 12.6 months (95% CI, 9.2 to 19.2).
Among 33 patients with previously treated, stable central nervous system metastases, the intracranial confirmed objective response rate was 33.3% (95% CI, 18.0 to 51.8).

safety.description: Treatment-related adverse events grade 3 or higher
safety.sourceQuote: Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 97.4% of the patients - grade 1 or 2 in 52.6% and grade 3 or higher in 44.8% (including two grade 5 events)

safety.description: Discontinuation due to treatment-related adverse events
safety.sourceQuote: and resulted in drug discontinuation in 6.9% of patients.

clinicalImplications.text: Established adagrasib as an active option in pretreated KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC, including activity in stable treated brain metastases.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Adagrasib showed intracranial responses in treated, stable brain metastases — relevant when choosing among KRAS G12C inhibitors.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 35658005. Abstract text strips the 'G12C' label.
